extracted.intended_audience: elementary and secondary school recipients (administrators and Title IX coordinators), school legal counsel, and policymakers implementing Title IX grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance on how elementary and secondary education (ESE) recipients must respond to reports of sexual harassment, including when grievance processes apply, required procedural protections, permissible flexibility for recipients, and training and timing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to any ESE employee triggers response obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice to any elementary or secondary school employee triggers the ESE recipient's response obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within these final regulations, a recipient must respond when any ESE employee has notice of conduct that could constitute sexual harassment under §106.30 that occurred in the recipient's education program or activity, against a person in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to minimize resource burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may adjust their procedures to minimize the amount of resources that must be spent with respect to each allegation of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations allow discretion to facilitate an informal resolution process and permit recipients to conduct the grievance process under time frames the recipient has designated as reasonable for an ESE environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal for imminent safety risks
rubrics_metrics.description: For emergencies posing imminent risks to any individual's safety recipients may invoke emergency removal procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency removal must be consistent with the terms of the final regulations; recipients may use emergency removal when necessary to protect safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility balanced with due process
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations offer significant flexibility to recipients while maintaining the appropriate balance between a recipient's duty to respond and due process protections for complainants and respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients retain discretion in many procedural choices while still being required to follow the core protections and obligations established by the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and predictability to encourage reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Having consistent, predictable rules for Title IX proceedings will likely make them less intimidating and encourage reporting by students and employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predictable rules also make it easier for legal counsel to advise recipients and may reduce costs over time as procedures become routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearings not required for ESE recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: ESE recipients are not required to use a hearing model to adjudicate formal complaints of sexual harassment under these final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an ESE recipient chooses to use a hearing model, it does not need to comply with §106.45(b)(6)(i) (which applies only to postsecondary institution recipients).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity and supportive assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing prevents schools from counseling students on grievance procedures or aiding and assisting parties with additional supports on an equal basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many provisions require only that schools provide an equal opportunity to the parties; recipients have flexibility to make the process less formal or intimidating for students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental/guardian rights to act on behalf of parties
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.6(g) acknowledges the legal rights of parents or guardians to act on behalf of complainants, respondents, or other individuals with respect to exercising rights under Title IX, including participation in a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where parents/guardians have legal rights, they may accompany their child throughout the grievance process and may be selected as an advisor of choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant choice re supportive measures vs grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants may choose whether reporting leads only to supportive measures or also to a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must offer supportive measures to every complainant (i.e., person alleged to be the victim), regardless of whether a grievance process is initiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process navigable without attorney; right to advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: The grievance process is designed for students to navigate without legal representation, though every party has the right to an advisor of choice who may be, but need not be, an attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should design procedures so meaningful participation is possible without legal counsel; advisors may assist parties at every stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural rights to mitigate unfair advantage by resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Granting both complainants and respondents strong procedural rights (including the right to assistance and advice from an advisor of the party's choosing) helps mitigate the possibility of a party unfairly using financial resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaningful participation of both parties at every stage is required by the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion across multiple procedural choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients retain discretion regarding: training to give ESE employees about reporting; when Title IX Coordinator may sign a formal complaint; what supportive measures are appropriate; time frames; age-appropriate explanatory language in written notices; standard of evidence; whether Title IX Coordinator is investigator; use of informal resolution; additional grounds for appeal; remedies and sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These discretionary choices must still be exercised within the confines of the final regulations and apply equally to complainants and respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process required only upon formal complaint or Coordinator signature
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45 grievance process is required only when the recipient is in receipt of a formal complaint (filed by the complainant or signed by the Title IX Coordinator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the absence of a formal complaint the recipient's response must consist of offering supportive measures designed to preserve equal access and protect safety; the grievance process is not required when no formal complaint exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution permitted but not mandated
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations allow recipients the discretion to facilitate an informal resolution process but do not mandate that any recipient offer or facilitate informal resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal resolution has adequate limitations and protections for parties; recipients decide whether to offer it and under what terms, consistent with §106.45(b)(9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of evidence available in ESE (including clear and convincing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The clear and convincing evidence standard may be appropriate in the ESE setting; ESE recipients are not categorically prevented from adopting that standard to resolve formal complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations revised to reflect that clear and convincing is not per se inappropriate for ESE institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably prompt time frames; limited delays for good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(v) permits recipients to provide short-term delays or extensions of their reasonably prompt time frame for conclusion of the grievance process when based on 'good cause' (example: concurrent law enforcement activity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are not required to delay a grievance while law enforcement is pending; 'good cause' does not justify long or indefinite delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt response triggered irrespective of formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44 a recipient's prompt response to every complainant is triggered with or without the filing of a formal complaint and without awaiting the conclusion of a grievance process if one is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must offer supportive measures promptly upon notice of sexual harassment, independent of whether a formal grievance is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of sexual harassment and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The §106.30 definition of sexual harassment (including quid pro quo by an employee, severe/pervasive/objectively offensive conduct denying equal access, or Clery Act/VAWA sex offenses) is appropriate for ESE application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients remain free to address conduct that does not meet that definition under State law or their own code of conduct; Title IX regs apply only when §106.44(a) conditions are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapted Supreme Court framework with specific recipient obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations adopt and adapt the Supreme Court's Gebser/Davis framework to place on recipients specific legal obligations to support complainants while ensuring due process and First Amendment protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adaptation aims to both protect complainants and ensure recipient responses meet constitutional and fairness requirements; may reduce litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rape shield protections for complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations provide rape shield protections and deem questions and evidence regarding a complainant's prior sexual behavior irrelevant unless offered to prove someone else committed the alleged conduct or to prove consent regarding specific incidents with the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These protections apply in investigations and hearings to limit irrelevant or prejudicial inquiries into prior sexual history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements for Title IX personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and any person who facilitates an informal resolution process receive certain training under §106.45(b)(1)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must include definition of sexual harassment, scope of education program or activity, how to conduct investigations and grievance processes (including hearings, appeals, informal resolution), how to serve impartially (avoid prejudgment, conflicts of interest, bias), and (for investigators/decision-makers) how to determine issues of relevance. Training materials must not rely on sex stereotypes and must promote impartial investigations/adjudications; recipients may add trauma-informed components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final regulations do not supersede IDEA/Section 504/ADA
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not supersede the IDEA, Section 504, or the ADA and provide flexibility for recipients who must comply with both sets of obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may utilize regulatory flexibility in challenging cases requiring compliance with both Title IX and applicable disability laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to consolidate related formal complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(4) gives recipients discretion to consolidate formal complaints where allegations arise from the same facts and circumstances so a single grievance process might involve multiple complainants and/or respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation is discretionary and intended to promote efficiency where cases are factually linked.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSE live hearing and cross-examination requirements and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Where sexual harassment is alleged in a PSE education program/activity, §106.45(b)(6)(i) requires adjudication by a live hearing with cross-examination conducted by party advisors (including a recipient-provided advisor if a party lacks one).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the request of either party, hearings must allow parties to be in separate rooms with technology enabling simultaneous sight/hearing; parties may not personally question each other; decision-maker must determine relevance before any party must answer cross-examination; decision-maker must not rely on statements of a party who does not appear/be cross-examined, and must not draw inference from refusal to appear or be cross-examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for minors in PSE processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations contain protections that mitigate potential re-traumatization of minors at live hearings (e.g., separate rooms, technology, relevance determinations), and a complainant need not be subjected to cross-examination if decision-maker does not rely on the complainant's statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing precludes recipients from training investigators/decision-makers in best practices for interviewing/questioning minors, so long as training meets §106.45(b)(1)(iii) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility when outsourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations do not preclude recipients from outsourcing investigative and adjudicative responsibilities to outside contractors, but recipients remain responsible for compliance with the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are accountable for ensuring any outsourced work complies with regulatory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients should attempt compliance with State/local laws; regs control if conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients ought to seek to comply with all State and local laws consistent with the final regulations; if a conflict cannot be resolved the final regulations control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to add waivers or safe harbors; having to follow separate processes for Title IX and State disciplinary procedures is not considered a negative consequence by the Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal application of age-appropriate discretionary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may employ age-appropriate rules and approaches within the framework of the final regulations, provided such discretionary rules apply equally to complainants and respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to create separate processes for preschool/elementary/middle/high school to preserve consistency/predictability, but permits recipient discretion within the regulatory framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights to inspect/review evidence and investigative report
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations establish rights for ESE students to defend themselves, including the right to inspect and review all evidence directly related to the allegations (including exculpatory evidence) and the right to review the investigative report summarizing relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rights are part of due process protections granted equally to complainants and respondents; parties also have the right to pose written questions and follow-up questions to other parties and witnesses prior to a determination regarding responsibility.
